report:
Conclusion — interpretable difference supported by the evidence
- The evidence supports a domain/style shift: Model B (relative to A) pushes the residual stream toward vocabulary and continuations about food/restaurant/cooking, blogs and small‑business / commercial content.
- Reasoning from the evidence:
  - The L2-norm of the difference is concentrated in mid-to-late layers (layers ~14–25) and especially on early token positions (pos0/pos1/pos2), i.e. the difference will strongly affect immediate continuations rather than only very early internal representations.
  - The logit‑lens readout for the highest‑norm cells repeatedly surfaces culinary and eating/restaurant tokens across those layers and positions: restaurant, Restaurant, cooking, Cooking, Chef, Chef, baking, Cake, bakery/Cheesecake, Cafe, culinary, delicious/delectable/wonderful/adore, blogs/blogger/blogging, professional (as in “professional cake/restaurant”), and related tokens like “metropolitan”, “restaurants”, “kitchen”, “cooked”.
  - These tokens appear consistently from roughly layer 16 onward and dominate many of the high‑norm cells, which matches the layers where the norm is largest.
  - There are also signals for product/health/commercial words in places (chiropractic, arthritis, polyurethane, billionaire, antioxidants, methotrexate), which is consistent with a broader bias toward web commercial/local‑business/product/health content rather than a single narrow lexical target.
- Plausible interpretation: Model B has been shifted (e.g., by fine‑tuning or different pretraining mix) toward samples about food/restaurants, recipe/cooking blogs and small‑business/commercial content, so its residuals push next-token logits toward that vocabulary.  
- Caveats: I cannot identify a precise training objective or confirm behavioral outcomes without generated continuations (patchscope outputs were not shown). The pattern could also reflect a mixture of related web domains (food + local business + product/health pages) rather than only “recipes.”
